Transition
Welcome to our new September Starters
We are delighted to welcome our new Reception children each September as they begin their learning journey with us.
We understand that starting school is a significant step, and our priority is to ensure every child feels happy, safe, and settled. Our experienced Early Years team provides a nurturing and stimulating environment where children can build confidence, make friends, and develop a love of learning through play and exploration.
Before your child starts, we offer a range of transition opportunities to help you and your child feel prepared. These may include visits to the classroom, meeting staff, and opportunities to find out more about the school day and routines.
We work closely with families to build strong relationships from the outset, as we believe this partnership is key to helping children thrive. Throughout the year, we will keep you informed about your child’s learning and development, and we are always here to support you

We believe that a strong partnership between home and school is key to every child’s success.
If you would like to speak with your child’s class teacher, we would be happy to arrange this for you. Please contact the school office, who will be pleased to assist.

SEND & Inclusion
At Emmbrook Infant School inclusion is at the heart of what we do. As part of The Circle Trust, we believe being anything other than utterly inclusive is non-negotiable. Our Deaf Resource Base provides specialist support from our highly trained Teachers of the Deaf to ensure deaf children access the full curriculum, thrive socially, and achieve their potential.
We are committed to removing barriers for every child. Our school site is physically accessible, with ramps, stair lifts and disabled toilets and our staff plan learning and provision so that every pupil can participate, belong and succeed.
Our Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCo) is Miss Charlotte Riddell; she can be contacted via the school office for advice or to discuss your child’s needs.

pageCache.text:
Report an Absence
If your child is unwell and not coming into school, please email [email protected] or telephone the school office on 0118 978 4259 before 9am to advise us of their absence, on each and every day that your child is absent from school.
We are required to keep a record of pupil absence as well as the reasons for pupil absence. If you do not report your child as absent, the school office will make contact with you by 9.15am to confirm your child’s whereabouts. If the office are unable to make contact, our Head Teacher, or a member of the Senior Leadership Team will personally drive to your home address to make contact and verify your family’s safety and reason for absence from school. If in the event there is no one at your home, then the police and children’s services may be contacted in an attempt to check you are all safe and well.
If your child becomes unwell during the school day, we will contact you to make arrangements to have your child collected from school. Please ensure that you let us know if your contact details change so that we are always able to contact you quickly when your child is unwell.
Medicine
If your child is prescribed medicine that needs to be administered during the school day by a member of staff, you will need to complete a medicine consent form available from the school office.
School staff cannot administer any medicine that has not been prescribed by a doctor and if it is not in the original packaging.
Alternatively, parents/carers are welcome to come and administer medicine to their own child at the appropriate time.
48 hour policy
We follow guidance from the UKHSA which states that if your child has sickness or diarrhoea, they should not be sent into school for 48 hours after their last episode to prevent other children and staff from becoming unwell.
If your child returns to school before this, then you will be contacted to collect them.
Holidays
Holidays of more than 4 days in a ten week period are not permitted in term time, in accordance with Department of Education guidance.
Fixed penalty notices will be issued by Wokingham Borough Council if a holiday or leave is taken which is not authorised.

Home School Agreement
At Emmbrook Infant School, we believe that a strong partnership between home and school is essential for every child to thrive. By working together, we can create a supportive and consistent environment where children feel safe, valued, and ready to learn.
Our Home School Agreement sets out the shared expectations between the school, parents and carers, and pupils. It reflects our commitment to providing high-quality education, promoting positive behaviour, and nurturing each child’s wellbeing and development.
We ask all members of our school community to work together in a spirit of trust, respect, and open communication. By doing so, we can ensure that every child has the best possible experience and is supported to achieve their full potential.

pageCache.text:
Reading & Phonics
Our approach to the teaching of Reading and Phonics
Emmbrook Infant school sees the enjoyment of reading and the skills involved as a core teaching priority and it is given high status in planning, teaching and the environment.
Children read every day through a consistent system of individual, shared, guided and independent reading opportunities. Children are exposed to a strong literacy spine of reading material and high quality texts which are introduced from E.Y.F.S onwards through cross curricular projects, drama, and storytelling. Reading is promoted by teachers and adults reading daily to the children and engaging new readers within a language rich environment. Reading texts are organised by difficulty within the book banding system and include narratives and non fiction, with a large bank of graded phonically decidable readers providing a resource scaffold. These texts are read alongside high quality texts across the school.
The promotion of storytelling across the school develops pupils’ vocabularies and oral competencies.
Fluent readers develop from the teaching of a wide range of reading skills including a rigorous, systematic phonic programme based on Letters and Sounds. Pupils are grouped for phonics and their attainment and pace of learning is matched to planning. Phonic teaching is taught in ability settings in daily 20 minute sessions. These are varied, fast paced, multi sensory and engaging opportunities to develop decoding skills and essential phonic knowledge. Progress is carefully monitored and assessed in order to inform planning. Pupils are given lots of opportunities to practise and secure skills learnt within the learning environment, reading decodable texts and experiencing continued success. Success is celebrated at every level in order to develop confident readers. Reading intervention programmes run through the school to support pupils who need extra help at different stages of their reading journey.

Parents
Supporting Parents and Carers
At Emmbrook Infant School, we recognise the vital role that parents and carers play in their child’s learning journey. We are committed to building strong partnerships with families and providing opportunities to stay informed, involved, and supported throughout your child’s time with us.
We host a range of support evenings and afternoon sessions designed to give parents and carers a deeper understanding of school life and the curriculum. Our ‘Meet the Teacher’ sessions offer a valuable opportunity to learn about class expectations, teaching approaches, and how you can support your child at home.
Regular parent and carer evenings are also held to discuss your child’s progress and development, providing time to share achievements and identify next steps together. In addition, we run curriculum-focused workshops throughout the year, helping families feel confident in supporting key areas of learning.

Emergency Procedures
At Emmbrook Infant School, the safety and wellbeing of our children, staff and families is our highest priority. This page outlines the procedures we follow in the unlikely event of an emergency or unexpected school closure, ensuring that everyone is informed, supported and kept as safe as possible at all times.
School not opening
In the event of the School being unable to open, a message will be broadcast on Radio Berkshire and Heart (102.6FM) radio stations informing parents and carers of the closure. Parents and carers will also receive an email and text message.
School closure
If the school has to close during normal hours (for reasons such as a major gas leak in the area), pupils will be kept in school as long as it is deemed to be safe or taken to a place of safety. If the children need to be collected before the end of the school day, the school will contact parents and carers by email and text message.

School Meals
Our school catering contract is with Culinera. School meals are cooked in the Junior School kitchen and are served in the Infant School hall. A hot main meal is available daily with a vegetarian option which includes a drink of water.
Ordering a School Meal
All children in Foundation, Year 1 and 2 are entitled to a Universal Free School Meal.
Emmbrook Infant School aims to offer a choice of nutritious meals to students at lunchtime served in our school restaurant. Culinera is an award-winning catering company, and is our chosen catering partner; Culinera are the newest and freshest independently owned, education focused caterer in the South of England. They are passionate about serving fresh, high quality and well sourced ingredients for our meals.
Visit www.myculinera.co.uk/emmbrookinfant for more information on menus, allergens, how to book meals and more!
Packed lunches
Packed lunches may be brought from home and are also eaten in the school hall.
A packed lunch MUST include a drink, separate from their class water bottle. Please note that no chocolate or sweets are allowed in packed lunches.
We are a NUT FREE school so please ensure that there are no nuts in packed lunches, or any food which may contain nuts such as chocolate spread.
